## Objective
Implement support for `datetime.timedelta` values in the `max_age` argument of `TimestampSigner.unsign`, `TimestampSigner.validate`, `TimedSerializer.loads`, and `TimedSerializer.loads_unsafe` in the ItsDangerous library.

- Accept `int`, `float`, `datetime.timedelta`, or `None` for `max_age`
- Preserve integer-second and `None` behavior and signed-token format
- No new runtime dependencies
- Update type annotations, docstrings, and `docs/timed.rst`
- Add regression tests in `tests/test_itsdangerous/test_timedelta_max_age.py`
- Only modify: `src/itsdangerous/timed.py`, `docs/timed.rst`, `tests/test_itsdangerous/test_timedelta_max_age.py`

## Decisions
- Created a module-level helper `_max_age_to_seconds()` to convert `max_age` to float seconds
- The age comparison uses `age > max_age_secs` (not `>=`) so an age equal to the limit is valid
- Future timestamps raise `SignatureExpired` when a finite age limit is supplied

  - `test_timedelta_expired` tests — `time.sleep(1.1)` may not be sufficient on this system

- The `_max_age_to_seconds()` helper converts `timedelta` via `.total_seconds()` and returns `float`
- The `unsign` method computes `age = self.get_timestamp() - ts_int` (integer), then compares `age > max_age_secs` (float)

For repeated anchors supply location={evidence_key: focus.evidence_key, line: inspected line, end_line: optional inclusive last line}; old must match exactly once within those inspected lines. Stale hashes/locations fail. After three equivalent failures use a DIFFERENT unique anchor or inspected location; another equivalent failure stops inference, even after reinspection. create requires expected_sha256=absent and old empty.
